# shop

A Go web service generated by [gobento](https://github.com/Tales-of-zuna/gobento).

## Run

```sh
go run ./cmd/shop
```

The server listens on port 8080; set `PORT` to change it. It connects to the
database named by `DATABASE_URL`, as described in [Database](#database).

```sh
curl localhost:8080/health
curl -X POST localhost:8080/items -d '{"name":"first"}'
curl localhost:8080/items
```

## Test

```sh
go test ./...
```

## Layout

The code follows domain-driven design in a ports-and-adapters layout: the
domain is at the center, the application layer runs the use cases on it, and
every piece of input and output is an adapter around them.

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cmd/shop` | Entry point: configuration and wiring of every layer |
| `internal/domain` | Domain: the `Item` entity, the rules for item names, and the `ItemStore` port |
| `internal/app` | Application: `ItemService`, which runs the item use cases and checks the domain rules |
| `internal/adapters/httpapi` | HTTP adapter: the router, the items handlers, and `/health` |
| `internal/adapters/persistence` | Persistence adapter: data access, implementing `ItemStore` |
| `internal/adapters/database` | Database adapter: connection and schema, used by the persistence adapter |

Dependencies point inward: the adapters and `app` import
`domain` and use or implement its ports, the adapters never
import `app`, and `domain`
imports no other package of the project. Only `cmd/shop` knows
every package and connects them: the HTTP adapter gets the application
service, which stores items through the persistence adapter.

The HTTP adapter depends only on the `domain.ItemStore`
port, which the application service implements. When the use cases grow
beyond storing and listing, give the handlers an interface of their own with
the service's methods. The handlers encode `domain.Item`
directly; when the API and the domain diverge, add response types to
`internal/adapters/httpapi`.

### Adding an aggregate

To add, for example, orders next to items:

1. Add `order.go` to `internal/domain` with the `Order` entity, its
   rules, and an `OrderStore` port. Once the domain holds several aggregates,
   give each one a package of its own, such as `internal/domain/order`.
2. Add an `OrderService` to `internal/app` for the order use cases. If
   they need items, give the service the `ItemStore` port, never an adapter.
3. Implement `OrderStore` in `internal/adapters/persistence`, following the items
   store, and add its tables to the schema in `internal/adapters/database`.
4. Add the order handlers to `internal/adapters/httpapi` and their routes to
   `NewRouter`, and in `cmd/shop/main.go` create the store and the
   service and pass the service to the router.

## API

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | `200` with `{"status":"ok"}` |
| `GET /items` | `200` with a JSON array of items, oldest first |
| `POST /items` with `{"name":"..."}` | `201` with the created item |

Errors are JSON objects such as `{"error":"name is required"}`:

- `400` when the body is not exactly one JSON object with a non-empty `name`
  (unknown fields and data after the object are rejected);
- `413` when the body is larger than 1 MiB;
- `500` when storage fails. The details are logged, not sent to the client.

## Database

The application stores its data in SQLite, through the pure-Go driver
modernc.org/sqlite, so it builds without a C compiler. `DATABASE_URL` is the
database file path or a modernc.org/sqlite connection string; by default it is
`shop.db` in the working directory (`DefaultURL` in
`internal/adapters/database`).

Tests need no setup: `internal/adapters/database/dbtest` gives every test an
empty database file of its own in a temporary directory.

### Schema

`internal/adapters/database/schema.sql` is embedded in the binary and applied
every time the application starts. It uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it
creates missing tables but never changes existing ones: it is not a migration
system. Before you change the schema of a database that already holds data,
add a migration tool or change the existing tables by hand.

## Changing queries

Data access is generated by [sqlc](https://docs.sqlc.dev/) from
`internal/adapters/persistence/queries.sql` and the schema in
`internal/adapters/database/schema.sql`, with sqlc's
`sqlite` engine, so write queries in that SQL dialect;
`sqlc.arg(name)` declares a parameter in any dialect. The generated code in
`internal/adapters/persistence/sqlcgen` is committed; do not edit it by hand. After
changing the schema or the queries, regenerate it:

```sh
go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate
```
